The Ossuary of Ayem: Wayward Servants
A precious ring was stolen from an internment site in the catacombs. The family of the deceased is very upset, and the Prefect of Ayem, Tarvyn Selvi, is seeking information.
Prefect Selvi informed me that multiple heirlooms have been reported missing from the catacombs. He suspects the thief may be a member of the Order of Ghosts.
I agreed to help Prefect Selvi investigate the missing heirlooms. I should speak to Boril Uvelen of the Tribunal Temple for more information.
Boril Uvelen directed me to speak with one of the Order of Ghosts scribes, who keep records of all donations, to confirm whether or not the ring was delivered along with its owner's remains.
Brelyna Hleran, a scribe of the Order of Ghosts, confirmed the delivery of remains. However, there is no mention of any ring in the report. She has given me a copy to take back to Prefect Selvi.

Guardian Darethi confessed to the thefts, but he claims to be working under the direction of Boril Uvelen, the head priest of Ayem. Guardian Darethi asked me to search Uvelen's private quarters for evidence that I can present to Prefect Selvi.
Guardian Darethi promised to surrender himself to the guards.
I delivered the ring to Prefect Selvi and informed him of Guardian Darethi's confession. Prefect Selvi asked me to provide evidence of Boril Uvelen's guilt.
I refused Boril Uvelen's proposal.
I decided not to help Prefect Selvi investigate the missing heirlooms.
I delivered the scribe's report to Prefect Selvi and ended my investigation of the missing heirlooms.
I delivered the ring to Prefect Selvi and ended my investigation of the missing heirlooms.
I delivered the ring to Prefect Selvi and informed him of Guardian Darethi's confession. I chose to end my investigation of the missing heirlooms.
I provided Prefect Selvi with enough evidence to incriminate Boril Uvelen.
I accepted Boril Uvelen's proposal. He has opened the services of a fence to me as a token of his gratitude. I should seek out Teryne Sadaves in the Bone Pit.
I killed Golam Darethi in the catacombs. He has taken his secrets to the grave.
One of the surviving Ghosts gave me a Bleeding Skull they found on the Sixth House altar.
I showed the Prefect the strange skull a Ghost gave me, but I didn't give it to him.
I gave the Prefect the strange skull a Ghost gave me. He helped me identify it as the life saving artifact - the Bleeding Skull.
Order of Ghosts: Remains Donation Registration Form
Airen Dara asked me to delivery a Remains Donation Registration Form to an elderly lady named Musa Yahaz in Gnisis for her to sign and confirm the registration.
I forged the signature of Musa Yahaz.
I visited Musa Yahaz and asked her to sign the registration form but she would like to sign it later. I should check back with her tomorrow.
Musa Yahaz didn't seem to remember that I visited her yesterday. She said she didn't leave the hut so if I really gave her the registration form, it should still be in the hut.
I found the registration form. It was not signed.
I found a note in Musa Yahaz's hut that says her name is Assimusa Yahazamibaal.
Musa Yahaz signed the registration form.
I gave Airen Dara the form with my forged signature.
I gave Airen Dara the form with Musa Yahaz's signature.
I gave Airen Dara the form with Assimusa Yahazamibaal's genuine signature.
Memento Mori: The Pilgrimage of the Dead

I have read "The Pilgrimage of the Dead" and have learned that there are three shrines on Red Mountain each dedicated to a god of the Tribunal. The shrines are located within the Great Ossuaries of the Ghostfence. Pilgrims may receive powerful blessings from these shrines. If I wish to embark on this pilgrimage, I can travel to the Ghostgate first to receive a prayer and a pilgrim's charm from the Commander of the Order of Ghosts, or I may travel to the shrines directly.

As I have decided to embark upon the Pilgrimage of the Dead, Adansa Kren, the Commander of the Order of Ghosts, has said a prayer for me before I depart on my journey to the three ossuaries. The Commander has also bestowed upon me a pilgrim's charm - a small amulet with a light enchantment - so that I may brave the darkness of the catacombs.

I have returned to Adansa Kren at Ghostgate after completing the Pilgrimage of the Dead. Commander Kren thanked me for honoring the Dunmer ancestors and also gave me a sacred rapier of the Order of Ghosts, as a gift in recognition of my tribute paid to the ancestors.
The Ossuary of Seht: A Broken Clock

The Shrine at the Ossuary of Seht has lost power. The replacement fuse needed to repair it is in the possession of a bone-cleaning centurion. I've agreed to help the Acolytes of Clockwork track down their runaway automaton, which was last seen heading into the Eastern Catacombs. The head of the Acolytes also indicated that he did not want to ask the Prefect of Seht for help. I wonder if she has anything to say on this matter.
Diraynia Sathil, the Prefect of the Ossuary of Seht has requested that I return the fuse to her instead of the Acolytes once I've found it. She has offered a reward if I am able to find it for her.
I have given the fuse to Prefect Sathil. She seemed quite pleased, but I fear the Acolytes of Clockwork will be very upset with me if I bring it up with them.
I restored power to the Shrine at the Ossuary of Seht.
After pushing the matter, Acolyte Hledri tossed a few Dwarven coins my way for my services, and has asked me to go away.
It seems that my reward is the Acolytes of Clockwork's gratitude and nothing else.
I decided not to help the Acolytes of Clockwork.
I have prayed at the Shrine of the Reborn at the Ossuary of Ayem and received a blessing from the Lady of Mercy.
I have prayed at the Shrine of the Altar at the Ossuary of Seht and received a blessing from the Clockwork God.
I have prayed at the Shrine of the Body at the Ossuary of Vehk and received a blessing from the Warrior-Poet.
I have met a half-Altmer, half-Dunmer member of the Order of Ghosts, at the Great Ossuary of Vehk. He had a lot to say about his background.
I have returned the skull of Varlix Rendereth to the Ossuary of Seht.
The Ossuary of Vehk: As Above, So Below

The Prefect at the Ossuary of Vehk has asked me to help the troops in the Western Catacombs fight back against a recent incursion from the Sixth House. There, I need to kill a Sixth House priest named Dagoth Nasro.
I spoke with Sergeant Llevi. The powerful Sixth House priest called Dagoth Nasro was reported to be invulnerable by the troops.
Dagoth Nasro says Dagoth Ur and the Sixth House will free Morrowind of foreign rulers and divine pretenders, and the false gods will reap the ruin of the wall of sin that they have built.
I have killed Dagoth Nasro, but none of the Ghosts have survived.
Dagoth Nasro is dead.
I have helped the troops kill Dagoth Nasro.
I have returned and reported to the Prefect.
Order of Ghosts: Pilgrimage
Order of Ghosts: Gather Remains

The Commander of the Order of Ghosts Adansa Kren has given me my first duty assignment. I need to collect the remains of the recently deceased. For more specific details on the task, I should ask assistant Airen Dara.
Airen Dara gave me the list of name of the recently deceased and the persons whom I need to collect their remains from.
I need to collect the remains of Feril Elval from Bolyn Elval in Ald'ruhn and the remains of Ravila Neryon from Garry in Maar Gan,
I have returned to the Hall of Ghosts with both the remains of Feril Elval and Ravila Neryon.
I have returned to the Hall of Ghosts with both the remains of Feril Elval and a guar.
I have returned to the Hall of Ghosts with both the remains of Feril Elval, Ravila Neryon, and a guar.
I have collected the remains of Feril Elval, Bolyn Elval's brother.
The Temple priest in Maar Gan gave the key to Garry's room and asked me to take the kwama eggs to him.
I gave Garry some kwama eggs.
Garry gave me a key to his hut. He begged me to not take the remains of Ravila Neryon away from him but the remains of a guar in his hut instead.
I have collected the remains of Ravila Neryon, Garry's partner.
I have collected the remains of a guar.

That's the Selaro amulet! And you found it in Uvelen's quarters? I will have him apprehended for questioning immediately. Though I suspect the s'wit may already be on his way back to his family's gardens in Mournhold. Thank you, %PCRace. You have done the Order of Ghosts a great service during these troubled times. Here, your reward.
Yes, have you found anything?

Good. Go to the Bone Pit and look for Teryne Sadaves. She'll pay you well for any trinkets you might find in the catacombs. Oh, and I'd steer clear of that bore Selvi if I were you. He'll surely catch wind of our new friendship soon enough. There are Ghosts in these walls, after all.

My, my... you're direct, aren't you? Good. Give me the amulet. No one will believe Golam Darethi's word over mine. He is a drunkard and a thief, and I am the head priest of this Temple. There are more like him who lurk in the shadows. And they know their place. If you do me this favor, I will open their services to you.
Then stop wasting my time. What? Did you expect me to fight you before my Lady? Go on, run along to Selvi with your baseless accusations.

Then stop wasting my time. What? Did you expect me to fight you before my Lady? Go on, run along to Selvi with your baseless accusations. No one will believe Golam Darethi's word over mine. He is a drunkard and a thief, and I am the head priest of this Temple. Begone, before I call the guards on you!

Give me the amulet. No one will believe Golam Darethi's word over mine. He is a drunkard and a thief, and I am the head priest of this Temple. There are more like him who lurk in the shadows. And they know their place. If you do me this favor, I will open their services to you.
Please, did you really just come here to gloat? I'm sure we can come to a... mutually beneficial arrangement.

These grand ossuaries were built to comfort the Dunmer with ritual, but it's a distraction. You, me, and every last soul on this damnable island, we're all just kindling for the fire. And that fire is burning out. The Ghostfence is not a testament to Almsivi's greatness but a sign of their weakness! No matter how high the Order stacks their precious bones, it will eventually fall, and the forces of Red Mountain will spill forth. I, for one, intend to enjoy life's pleasures to the fullest until then!

An outlander like you could never understand. For time immemorial, my family has devoted themselves to the Temple, secure in the knowledge that they belong to the favored House of the Gods. But this isn't Mournhold, %PCRace. We live on the edge of Oblivion. At first, I resented my family for sending me here, to this forsaken land of ash and fire. Was I really such a disappointment? But I should be thanking them, for now I see the truth!
Did he? And did he weep over his family, too? I'm glad to be rid of that pathetic fool. I told him to get rid of that blasted ring, but instead he chose to wear it as a weight around his neck.
Well, aren't you a clever little %PCRace! But why are you here, exactly? It doesn't appear that I've been clapped in irons yet. Surely there's a reason for that?
Do you think yourself a clever little %PCRace, flaunting that amulet before me? Guards! Thief!
Do you think yourself a clever little %PCRace, flaunting that amulet before me? Golam Darethi is dead, and his secrets have died with him. Begone, before I call the guards on you!

Selvi suspects a thief is among us? Preposterous. More likely than not, the widow simply misplaced the ring. Grief clouds the mind terribly, you know. Luckily, ink and quill are not quite so vulnerable to the same influences. If the ring was delivered as the widow claims, our scribes will surely have a record of it. Look for Indrasa Davos or her apprentice, Brelyna. Their office is on the second floor of this tower. May Almsivi guide your steps.

How could you return it to Prefect Sathil? Now our Lord's shrine will remain in darkness for years to come, all because of her narrow-mindedness and your foolishness. I hope you're proud of yourself, %PCRace.

An unsophisticated eye might mistake it for the standard Dwemer Tube, but be warned, only the Acolyte variant will suffice for our purposes. The fuse seems to have been stuck fast within the runaway automaton's cleaning apparatus. Oh, I do hope they haven't developed a taste for scrap metal...
You may make the Pilgrimage of the Dead as often as you wish, %PCName. May the spirits guide you.

Here. This is a sacred rapier of the Order of Ghosts. I do not part with this possession lightly, %PCName. It is normally presented only to select members of our order for exemplary service, but you are the first outlander in many, many years to complete the Pilgrimage of the Dead. While you carry this weapon, an ancestral spirit will serve as your guardian and protector. Bear it with honor. Go now with my appreciation. I thank you for the respect you have given to our ancestors.

Yes, I see it now. I can feel the blessings of Almsivi upon you, %PCName. I can tell that you have already completed the Pilgrimage of the Dead. Wait here a moment. Let me retrieve something from my quarters.
You know now what you must do, %PCName. Go now, and may Almsivi go with you.

As long as the dead are not disturbed you should be able travel with ease. Some encounters will be inevitable of course, but if your heart is true, Almsivi may guard you on your path. If you wish, I may also offer you a prayer and a pilgrim's charm for your journey.

If you wish to complete the pilgrimage you must travel to the Great Ossuary of Ayem, the Great Ossuary of Seht, and the Great Ossuary of Vehk, and offer a prayer at the Shrine of the Reborn, the Shrine of the Altar, and the Shrine of the Body respectively. You may complete the pilgrimages in any order you see fit. You may also travel over land, but I highly recommend you make use of the catacombs instead.

It is a sacred rite performed by all members of my order, but pilgrims from all walks of life undertake it. It was once a far more popular pilgrimage route, but as the blight waxes, it seems the faithful wane. Not many are willing to get so close to the dangers of Red Mountain even in the relative safety of the catacombs.

Of course you have come here on the Pilgrimage of the Dead. I see no other reason why any self-respecting person would come here and visit this temple of blasphemy the Acolytes have built for themselves.

So it is the Pilgrimage of the Dead that has brought you to this place. It is a sacred journey that you have chosen to undertake, outlander, so see that you treat the dead with the proper respect that they deserve.
I've of course undertaken the pilgrimage many times, myself. My best advice to a first time pilgrim? Stay out of the side passages, and you'll do just fine.
I'm afraid we are in far too dire straits at the moment, and too much in need of aid ourselves, to provide any help to traveling pilgrims. I'm sorry.

It pleases me to see an outlander take an interest in our customs. The fact that you have traveled this far out to the Ossuary of Vehk proves your dedication. Continue to walk forward faithfully, and Almsivi may yet guide your steps.
The Ordinator Grand Commander Ralyn Othravel is upstairs. Rilvase Avani is the priest of the Temple. The Grand Commander of the Order of Ghosts, Adansa Kren, is downstairs, in the Hall of Ghosts.

They are the dedicated servants of our Lord Sotha Sil. They are a small order and can be found only at the Ossuary of Seht. They seek to surround themselves with Lord Sil's sphere of Clockwork, and attempt to do so through the use of Dwemer technology. Some in my order have taken to calling the Ossuary of Seht: the New Clockwork City. It is truly a sight to behold. The opinion on them and their methods is greatly divided in the Temple, but they hold Lord Vivec's favor and have not been excommunicated.

They've drifted far from the sacred ideals of the Temple. This fact has been realized for centuries by the priesthood in Necrom, but the priests of Vivec City still hold them in high esteem, and Mournhold remains neutral on the matter. If Lord Sil Himself deigned to address their sins, He would order them to be disbanded at once. Mortals were never meant to possess this sort of power. It was this hubris that led to the destruction of the Dwemer, and why Sil hides His own creations away from the world.
We are the true and willing servants of the God of Clockwork. He created our order and granted us leave to pursue knowledge in His name.

The Acolytes of Clockwork are an ancient order, though our numbers have dwindled greatly throughout the centuries, and we now number less than a dozen in total. As the Recorder of the Acolytes, it is my duty to preserve our history for future generations.
Watch. Wonder. Build. Tear Down. We strive to live by these pure and simple commandments of our Clockwork God.
The Rendereth clan has long been a part of the Acolytes of Clockwork. I hope to make my ancestors proud in the work that I do here.

We are hidden throughout the land. As above, so below. Our Lord gives glory to his faithful servants. When the hour of ascent approached, he wholeheartedly welcomed death as his soul is still among us.

At the Shrine of the Reborn, we honor the dead's sacrifice to be reborn as spirits to defend us in this life. We know we will all one day join their ranks, so we, too, must dedicate ourselves to them. You must offer a sanctified skull taken from a fallen ancestral guardian of the catacombs to the shrine. You need not show remorse for this deed. A guardian who would attack a pilgrim and fall has long outserved its purpose. The skull will be reconsecrated by priests of Almalexia directly into the Ghostfence.
You stand now in the sanctum of the Shrine of the Reborn. Please show it the proper respect it deserves.
This shrine is dedicated to Mother Almalexia, %PCRace. Treat it with respect.
Head upstairs if you are looking for the shrine, outlander.
The shrine can be found in the temple, which itself is located in the southern wing of this ossuary.
[The man cried silently and gives you a key.]

[The man cries inconsolably.] Pain afflicts no more when it comes to be a part of life. Oh, gods! Sorrow is erased when man is overwhelmed by sorrow; so many misfortunes fell upon me that I became trouble-free. Just take it, the remains.
Could you take the urn in our hut instead? It's, it's guar remains. Please.
I know. I know that she's not there. I think I'm dying. [Garry burst into spasms of sobbing.] Just take it, the remains.
Her remains... I saw her in a dream. She'll come visit me again, if you don't take her away.
Her remains... I saw her in a dream. She'll come visit me again. Why did you take her away?

My brother was a man of great renown. He died nobly and honourably. And that is, he lived in the faith and died in the faith. His remains is in this urn. It is an invaluable blessing that he could serve the living gods and his nation even in the afterlife. Brother, you truly were the strongest person I know. I am so grateful for and so proud of you.
Leave me alone please.
Am I hungry or just sad?

Yes. He has been living here for a week or so now. You're here for Ravila Neryon's remains? Emm, you should be able to open the door with this key. Also, take these kwama eggs to Garry for me, will you?

This shrine honors the Ghostfence and Ossuaries, altars of a sort in their own right. They were both designs made first by Sotha Sil, hence His association with this shrine. Pilgrims may offer Dwemer scrap metal to the shrine, as the ghostfence would have never been possible without Sil's own studies of their technology. The Acolytes of Clockwork will use any scrap metal left at the shrine in their own research.
If you are a pilgrim, approach the shrine. Be sure to have some scrap metal in hand.
You'll find the shrine in the lowest level of the Ossuary, near the doors to the catacombs.

The Shrine of the Body represents the precious gift of life. As all of our days are fleeting, we must cherish what few we have. Pilgrims leave pomegranates at the shrine which help to bolster the food supplies for the ossuary. Food and water are valuable resources in the Ashlands, and pomegranates contain both. Pomegranate trees may grow rarely on Vvardenfell now, but the easiest place to find some would be the grove at the Ossuary of Vehk itself.

Do you have a pomegranate to leave as an offering, Pilgrim? If not, use the eastern door here to head outside to the grove and pick one. Please do not pick the ones here in the shrine, as these plants are sacred.
The shrine is upstairs, outlander.
The shrine is housed in the ossuary's colossal tower. Head outside and across the bridge to enter the tower.

Technically, no. Here, 300 drakes. This is more than enough. Ask around in Gnisis where she is. Musa Yahaz. She should be an elderly Dunmer lady according to the logs here. Return the document back to me once it is signed.

Ask around in Gnisis where she is. Musa Yahaz. She should be an elderly Dunmer lady according to the logs here. Return the document back to me once it is signed. 200 drakes should cover your travel expense.

Good, here is the list of name of the recently deceased and the one whom you'll need to collect their remains from. While you're out in the field, surely you would be willing to deliver this letter to Musa Yahaz in Gnisis and ask her to sign the form to confirm her registration with the remains donation,

My fellow Acolytes have seen you speaking with Prefect Sathil. We know that you have returned the fuse to her and she has since destroyed it. How could you betray the Lord of Clockwork so easily? Get out of my sight!

Yes, a Clockwork modification of the common Dwemeri spider. There are several, far more amenable specimens roaming this workshop. Within the central sanctification chamber, skulls are stripped of flesh until only the bone remains. A gruesome sight, but far preferable to choking on ash in a crematory.
So you've chosen to side with the Acolytes. I see now where you stand, %PCName. I have nothing more to discuss with you.
Whatever you do, do not return it to the Acolytes. Take it far away from here. Sell it, gift it to a Telvanni Magelord, keep it as a trophy... I don't care. Just don't return it to Hledri!

I applaud your efforts, outlander. I will be sure to include the recent malfunctions of both the machinery and automatons here in my next report to the mainland. With any luck, it will slowly chip away at the trust some in the Temple still place in the Acolytes. Here. Take this Temple coinage as your prize. Most shops do not accept them anymore, but they'll still buy them off you at a fair price as they are somewhat of a collector's item.
So, you managed to track the little menace down... Is that the Acolyte fuse? Quickly! Give it here.

Is that so? Listen. Give me the fuse instead of that blasphemous priest. I will dispose of it quietly, and it should be a few years before the Acolytes can develop another. In the meantime, Lord Sotha Sil's shrine will be free of that hideous display. Do this for me, and I will see that you are suitably rewarded for your efforts.

Don't tell me those Acolytes have asked you to help with their little escaped pet as well. They've had nothing better to do but bother the Order day in and day out about "restoring the shrine's wonderous clock." Pfft... The shrine is much better suited without all of those disgusting contraptions surrounding it. If it were up to me, I'd have that whole thing dismantled and removed.

Listen. If you find the fuse, bring it to me instead of that blasphemous priest. I will dispose of it quietly, and it should be a few years before the Acolytes can develop another. In the meantime, Lord Sotha Sil's shrine will be free of that hideous display. Do this for me, and I will see that you are suitably rewarded for your efforts.
You can enter the catacombs through the large door on the western side of this hall.

With the Blight gone, Dagoth Ur defeated, and the Ghostfence deactivated, I fear the Order's days are numbered, but I will continue to serve the ancestors until Lord Vivec or Lady Almalexia Herself command me to do otherwise.

As the Commander of the Order of Ghosts, it is my duty to ensure that our troops are well-supplied, well-trained, and ready to face any threat from Red Mountain. The blight grows stronger every day, and a small part of me fears that the Ghostfence might not hold forever... But I forget myself. Let us discuss another matter.

I joined the Order of Ghosts after I lost my family to the Blight. I just couldn't sit idly by as so many had chosen to do and watch the Sixth House bolster their forces on the mountain. I have served the Order with distinction for many years, and it is for that reason that I was chosen to serve as the Prefect of Ayem.

It was Sotha Sil who was the principle architect of the Ghostfence, the Ghostgate, the Great Ossuaries, and the catacombs, but it was our Lord Vivec who mandated the formation of the Order of Ghosts. The Ossuary of Vehk was the original home of the Order, but now our headquarters are at Ghostgate, and most of our troops are stationed at the Ossuary of Ayem.

I have not been with the Order of Ghosts for long, although I have the utmost respect for them. When there was a vacancy for the position of Prefect, here at the Ossuary of Seht, I was pulled from my post in Necrom as a captain of the Ordinators in Mourning. Alvu Sareleth recommended me to the position as she felt the Acolytes of Clockwork were drifting far from Necrom standard funerary practices. As soon as I arrived here, I quickly realized how correct she was.

We are a sacred order of the Tribunal Temple. We dedicate our lives to the defense of the Great Ghostfence, the Great Ossuaries of Ayem, Seht, and Vehk, and the catacombs deep beneath Red Mountain. We walk among the dead as one of them, for we might as well truly be of their ranks. We have consigned ourselves to our duty, and serve with honor.

The Ossuary of Ayem is dedicated to our Lady Almalexia and houses the Shrine of the Reborn. In addition to our order, it is maintained with the aid of the Ordinators and the Temple priesthood. Tarvyn Selvi is the Prefect of our order there. It is located northeast of Ald’ruhn as the racer flies. Follow the mountain path behind the Ald’ruhn Temple, and take the first left. Follow the trail a bit further and you will reach it.

The Ossuary of Ayem is the public face of both the Order of Ghosts, and of the Ghostfence Catacombs more generally. It is the only ossuary that is still visited daily by both pilgrims and mourners alike, due to its close proximity to Ald'ruhn. As its Prefect, I strive to maintain its image in these trying times. We must continue to hold the people's trust if the Order is to continue in its operations here.
It is a worthy house for the remains of the faithful servants of the Mother of Mercy.
Did you know the Ossuary of Ayem is home to one of the largest Tribunal Temples on all of Vvardenfell?
The Ossuary of Ayem was built over the ruins of an old Tribunal abbey. A few of the ruins are still standing on the hill between the ossuary and Ald'ruhn.
Follow the catacombs to the west to reach the Ossuary of Ayem.
Keep heading south and you will reach the Ossuary of Ayem.
The Western Catacombs connect the Ossuary of Vehk with the Ossuary of Ayem.
You can use the Southern Catacombs to travel to the Ossuary of Ayem from here. It's just a very short, safe, and easy trek to the west.

The Ossuary of Seht is dedicated to the Mage Sotha Sil and houses the Shrine of the Altar. It is smaller than the other ossuaries but served fervently by the Acolytes of Clockwork. Diraynia Sathil is the Prefect of the Order of Ghosts for Seht. To get there look for a small pass through the hills west of the Zainab Camp and head through it. Once you are in the Foyada, go due south. Pass the Sandus Ancestral Tomb on your left, and the ossuary will be just beyond.

The core structure of this ossuary is a fine example of Velothi architecture. It is constructed in a mixed style of a fane and a traditional Dunmeri ancestral tomb. However, it has largely been defiled by the Acolytes of Clockwork, who have installed Dwemeri structures and ornaments all over the place. Hopefully, I can clear these repulsive displays out of here one day, and restore its sanctity.
It is a magnificent temple of the Clockwork God, and I am pleased to serve as its chief attendant. Here we may watch, wonder, build, and tear down, just as a our Lord has commanded us to do.

It is the only dedicated Temple to Sotha Sil on all of Vvardenfell. We Acolytes of Clockwork are a bit unorthodox for most of the Temple priesthood, so we fulfill our small duty of maintaining this ossuary and a portion of the catacombs, and in return the Temple gives us leave to live here and pursue our own interests as we see fit. It is a mutually beneficial arrangement.
Have you come here to ponder on the glory of Clockwork, outlander? A most noble pursuit.
The ossuary's location was chosen for its proximity to the large Dwemer ruins nearby. From them we scavenge more than enough materials to continue our research and operations here.
Continue following these passageways to the east to reach the Ossuary of Seht.
You can use the southern catacombs to travel to the Ossuary of Seht from here.
The Eastern Catacombs will lead you to the Ossuary of Seht from here.

It is very difficult to reach over land, as all roads in the northern Ashlands are unmarked and lightly traveled, except by the ashlanders. Your best bet is just to use the catacombs. If you need to go over land, the only way I know how is to head southeast from Maar Gan using jump or levitation magic until you reach the Ghostfence. Keep following the Ghostfence east and you’ll eventually find it.

The Ossuary of Vehk is dedicated to the Warrior-Poet Vivec and houses the Shrine of the Body. It is the largest ossuary on Vvardenfell, in terms of the remains interred, but its isolated position means it is only served by a small contingent of Buoyant Armigers and a few members of our order. Trelian Ramoran is the current Prefect of Vehk.

It is my charge. We are flanked by the Sixth House on all sides, as they have taken over nearby Kogoruhn and Falasmaryon, and they can of course be found just on the other side of the Ghostfence as well. We are in an extremely vulnerable position out here, and our only resupply route is through the catacombs. We must remain steadfast and diligent, lest Dagoth Ur and his corrupted minions overrun us.
It's not much, but it's home.

The Great Ossuary of Vehk is the oldest of the three ossuaries of Red Mountain. It was constructed first as a counterbalance to Ghostgate, so that the Temple could have a strong presence on both the north and south sides of the Ghostfence.
The Death Netch outside will do you no harm. They're actually quite docile.
There are many ossuary pits dotting the landscape outside, around the Great Ossuary of Vehk.
The shrine tower of this ossuary can be seen for miles. It is an excellent landmark for navigating the Ashlands.
Keep heading north sera, and you will reach the Ossuary of Vehk in no time.
Take the Eastern Catacombs to travel to Vehk from here. Just mind the centurions along the way.
The Western Catacombs connect the Ossuary of Ayem with the Ossuary of Vehk.

The main tunnel leading west to the Ossuary of Ayem and east to the Ossuary of Seht meets the side tunnel connected to Ghostgate at a T-junction. The Fadathram Ancestral Tomb also can be accessed through one of the crypts in the west wing.

Ghostgate consists of two towers, the Tower of Dusk -- the west keep -- and the Tower of Dawn -- the east keep -- with a temple between the two towers, and a tunnel beneath the temple leading up Foyada Esannudan into Red Mountain. The Redoran hostel and Buoyant Armiger barracks are in the Tower of Dusk. The Temple services, the Ordinator barracks, and the Hall of Ghosts are in the Tower of Dawn. The pilgrimage shrine lies west of the stronghold along a path.

Search Uvelen's private quarters. He took the Selaro amulet for himself last week. A gaudy thing, set with an enormous emerald. He always had a taste for such baubles. If you bring Prefect Selvi evidence of Uvelen's guilt, he will see that justice is done. I know it. That Indoril s'wit cannot hide behind the robes of his House forever!
Wait. I may have no honor left, but I cannot allow that false priest to desecrate the dead any longer! Uvelen promised silence, as long as I kept his pockets full. And so I did. Almsivi forgive me!

Wait. I may have no honor left, but I cannot allow that false priest to desecrate the dead any longer! Uvelen caught me leaving the catacombs one night with ash-covered hands and a heavy pouch. I should have gone straight to the Prefect and took my licks. But the priest, his words were so sweet. He promised silence, as long as I kept his pockets full. And so I did. Almsivi forgive me!
As you wish, outlander.
Thank you, outlander. You have freed me of a heavy burden.
I swear on my ancestors, I will surrender myself to the guards. Please, just give me a moment alone to beg the dead for forgiveness.

Search the priest's private quarters. Uvelen took the Selaro amulet for himself last week. A gaudy thing, set with an enormous emerald. He always had a taste for such baubles. If you bring Prefect Selvi evidence of Uvelen's guilt, he will see that justice is done. I know it. That Indoril whelp cannot hide behind the robes of his House forever!

He disgraces the Blessed Mother with his presence! I should have gone straight to the Prefect and took my licks. But the priest, his words were so sweet. He promised silence, as long as I kept his pockets full. And so I did. Almsivi forgive me! I forgot my honor as a Ghost in a moment of weakness. Please, %PCRace, we cannot allow that false priest to desecrate the dead any longer!

The dead have no need of coin, but my children go hungry at night. Why should my wife have to beg the Temple for charity? Haven't I given enough? My life, my soul... After I die, she'll be lucky if the priests send her a knucklebone. It felt easy, too easy, to palm a few gold pieces here and there... but I got careless. That s'wit Uvelen saw me leaving the catacombs one night with ash-covered hands and a heavy pouch.

You have to understand... my children didn't recognize me when I came home. They're young, my wife said, and you're away for so long. But I know the truth. I'm a Ghost. I don't belong with the living. I belong here, in the darkness, with my friends who have joined the Great Fence before me. My wife, she looks me in the eyes and sees death staring back. So, I... I don't go home anymore... but I will not have my family think that I've abandoned them!
So this is how it ends... I have disgraced my ancestors and brought shame to my order. I am at your mercy, outlander.
No, I don't care to explain, outlander. I don't know anything about any ring, got it?
I don't know what you're talking about, outlander. You should leave this place before you get yourself killed.
Well, the ashes were delivered, but I don't see anything about a ring. Guardian Golam Darethi was assigned to donations that day. Here, you can take the report back to Prefect Selvi.

A ring? What are you -- oh! Look what you made me do! This scroll is completely ruined! Not that I understand why anyone should care about a little smudged ink in this place. Everything gets covered with ash, eventually. But seeing as I have to fetch a new scroll, I suppose I could look up this donation for you. When did you say the remains were delivered? Mmm-hmm. I'll be just a moment.
Did you find what you were looking for? I hope you didn't distract that fool girl from her duties.
What? No, I don't have time to help you with that. Speak to my apprentice, Brelyna Hleran, on the second floor of this tower.

There is no mention of the ring in the donation report? Just as I suspected, then. These vile accusations against the Order are merely the product of a troubled mind. I will be sure to offer the widow counsel if she returns to the Temple. May the Blessed Mother be a comfort to her in these dark days.
Have you asked the scribes for a record of the donation yet? That should put an end to this nonsense.
Of course, how could I forget? She was screaming loud enough to wake the dead. Emerald, with a silver band.

Yes, I had the pleasure of speaking with the mer's widow. Although I dare say the conversation was quite one-sided. Her words are not fit to be repeated before the Blessed Mother! May Almsivi forgive her impropriety. The widow swore on her late husband's ashes that she had personally handed his ring to the Ghost in charge of donations that day. Unfortunately, she could not recall their name. A pity.
So, a shred of honor still clings to your bones? I'm surprised. Now get out of my sight.
You have done the Order of Ghosts a great service during these troubled times. Here, your reward.

Uvelen? I'm not fond of the mer myself, but these are serious accusations. The head priest belongs to a powerful Indoril clan on the mainland. If I were to pursue this... Well, they could make my life very difficult. I'm afraid my hands are tied unless you bring me real evidence of Uvelen's guilt.

Yes, I was just informed that Guardian Darethi surrendered himself to the guards. As is our custom, he has been banished to the catacombs for the remainder of his time on Nirn. Let the ancestors be his judge. And this is the ring? Well done, %PCRace. Was there anything else you wanted to report?

Uvelen? I'm not fond of the mer myself, but these are serious accusations. The head priest belongs to a powerful Indoril clan on the mainland. If I were to pursue this... Well, they could make my life very difficult. Even if you were to find evidence, we no longer have Darethi's testimony to support his claims. I'm afraid my hands are tied. But here, a token of the Order's appreciation.

Yes, one of the runners just informed me of Guardian Darethi's death. I'm sure it couldn't be avoided. You never know what a rat will do when it's cornered. Still, I would have preferred for the Order to dispense its own justice. And this is the ring? Seems a small thing to have caused so much misery. Was there anything else you wanted to report?

The catacombs are no place for outlanders, %PCRace. But if you insist, the entrance to the Southern Catacombs is west of the crematorium, or the Bone Pit, as it's more commonly called. If you fail to return, I will assume you've joined the ranks of the dead and send my Ghosts in to clean up what's left of you. Oh, and you may hold on to the ring for now. Guardian Darethi might need a little... encouragement, if you want him to confess. Good luck.

You found the ring in Guardian Darethi's chest? This is incriminating evidence, indeed. I will send a cohort of guards to the Southern Catacombs immediately. We can only hope that Guardian Darethi will surrender peacefully.
Yes, I think we owe the mer that much. The Order of Ghosts barracks are housed in the northern tower. If Darethi is not there, he is likely on patrol in the Southern Catacombs.
This is the report? Hmm. There's no mention of a ring among the deceased's personal effects. And yet the widow claims to have handed it directly to Guardian Darethi...
Yes. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some letters to write.

I ask myself, why is an outlander interested in our affairs? Do you really enjoy the smell of moldering bones and grave dust so much? But if you speak truly, you'd do well to find our head priest, Boril Uvelen. He spoke with the widow after she discovered her late husband's ring missing. Quite the colorful conversation, I hear. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some letters to write.

It's not the first incident we've had, I'm afraid. Just last week the entire Selaro family was nearly up in arms over their mother's amulet or some other such trinket. What use do our ancestors have for such things? Forgive my blasphemy, but I've lost my taste for ritual having lived amongst the dead for so long. Still, these thefts are troubling. Common graverobbers tend to avoid the catacombs. I don't want to believe it, but the thief may be a Ghost.
Have you heard? The Sixth House have managed to tunnel into the Western Catacombs. By the Three! We're all going to die out here!
I've heard that Commandant Orethi was investigating possible necromancer activity in the Eastern Catacombs, but Prefect Ramoran has forbidden him from pursuing the matter further.
Diraynia Sathil, the new Prefect here, is constantly at odds with Tendryn Hledri, the head of the Acolytes of Clockwork. Seems she is not the biggest supporter of their methods.

Have you witnessed it with your own eyes? The glorious clock at the shrine of Lord Sotha Sil, has fallen as still as death. Tendryn Hledri, the head of our order, is in the Dwemer workshop right now, trying to restore it.

Did you hear that commotion in the Great Hall earlier? A widow came to pay respects at her husband's urn and started screaming something about a missing ring. I'm told she nearly came to blows with our head priest. I would like to have seen that! Tarvyn Selvi, the Prefect here, is seeking any information.
Prefect Selvi lost his wife and daughter to the Blight. He signed up with the Order not long after they were interred in the catacombs.
Rumor is that our head priest's family pulled some strings to get him the position. He's a member of House Indoril, from the mainland. But if that's true, why did they send him all the way out here?

Did you hear? Boril Uvelen and Prefect Selvi were arguing again. Not that I blame Selvi for losing his temper. I saw another shipment of imported goods being delivered to Uvelen's private quarters the other day.
%PCRank, smart people don't do things alone. You have my friendship.
[Sign.]
Isn't that an Ashlander name? [The old lady shakes her head, the reality of it all pressing down on her.] I need some rest.
So that's my name. Musa Yahaz. I think it's a nice name.
I don't remember my name, or who you are, or why I am signing this paper.
No. ... I think earlier I was waiting for the Temple priest to come visit me so I didn't leave the hut.
[She says with nervous laughter.] You know, I am not quite sure I remember that. I'm sorry, who are you?
Oh um, hmm... but I don't remember what that means. Well, I was waiting for...
Oh, don't be. Do I sign right here?
I'll read the broadsheet later. I have the rest of my life to cook dinners and read books and recite a little prayer.
Thank you. I'll read the form and sign it later.
Yes, the registration form. Don't forget it.
Someone in the services tower might know where to find him. The Order of Ghosts barracks are on the top floor.
Yes, I heard the news. I'd rather not talk about him right now...

Guardian Darethi is on patrol in the Southern Catacombs right now. He's been spending a lot of time down there lately, it seems. I'm worried about him. Spending too many waking hours in that kind of darkness does strange things to your mind.

I haven't seen him around lately, but you could check the barracks. Take the west stairwell from the second floor of this tower. He sleeps in the first bunk you'll come across at the top of the stairs.
Very cursed indeed.
This is the Bleeding Skull. A rare artifact. Worthy of any private collection, I am sure. I am fairly certain that the skull contains magical properties but sadly I have failed to identify any.
This is the Bleeding Skull. A rare artifact that can save one's life. If you don't mind it looking too ominous, carry it around like a lucky charm.
[The Prefect begins casting spells on the skull.]
Very strange indeed. May I have a closer look at that skull?
What?! I don't want any pomegranates... No pomegranates! No! No! No No! NO POMEGRANATES! NONE! I don't want them anywhere near here... Am I clear?! Say the rule again: NO POMEGRANATES! SAY IT!
The Prefect of Ayem can be found in his private quarters, just off the Great Hall.

You can usually find him by the Shrine of the Reborn. It's on the uppermost floor of the southern tower. If he's not there, he's probably in his quarters getting drunk on imported wine. You'd think the mer is bathing in that swill with the amount he orders every month. And here I can barely afford to keep my soldiers fed and their blades sharp!
No one has seen him around here in some time.
He's by the Shrine of the Reborn on the uppermost floor of this tower.
He gorges himself on wine and cakes while Ghosts die in the catacombs.
The head priest of Ayem can be found by the Shrine of the Reborn.
No one goes in but the Ghosts.

The Order recognizes you, %PCName. You are now %PCName the %NextPCRank. Remember that you can get supplies from the chest behind Airen's desk. Also, you are one of us now so you should have this. It's our uniform. Wear it with honor.
If you want to advance in the Order, you must dedicate more of your time and resources to serving our cause.
Bolyn Elval is in the Arobar Guard Quarters.
Bolyn Elval is one of Councilor Arobar's bodyguards.
This is the wall that divides the children of Veloth. We are the Sixth House servants of our Lord. A mighty army, unified to tear down the Ghostfence.
...Listen and you will see the love...
'Here,' Vivec said, 'is the last of the last. Within it the Sharmat waits.'
Love is under my will only.' The ending of the words is ALMSIVI.

Please accept our thanks for your selfless service during such challenging times. I know I said before that I promised you a handsome reward, but you'll have to forgive me. Already underfunded and understaffed, the ossuary cannot afford to lose any more equipment. But please accept this volume from the teachings of Vivec in lieu of a more proper reward.

We will forever honor our fallen heroes. Please accept our thanks for your selfless service during such challenging times. I know I said before that I promised you a handsome reward, but you'll have to forgive me. With such a great loss, the ossuary cannot afford to lose any more equipment.
We can take it from here. Thanks for the help. I found this strange skull on their altar. Looks like a unique artifact.

Dagoth Ur is the Awakened Lord of the Sixth House, come to cast down false gods. They will reap the ruin of the wall of sin that they have built. The great divide will fall and the ancient glory of Resdayn will be restored.
And may the glory of our Lord be upon his servant. Argh!
Serve your Lord, Dagoth Ur. The Sixth House is risen, and Lord Dagoth is its glory.
Follow me.

I'm Sergeant Llevi. Our goal is to take out their leader, a powerful Sixth House priest named Dagoth Nasro. The scout said that even though the priest and other Sixth House beasts haven't caused any major losses for the troops yet, our enemies seem almost completely invulnerable.
We have to hire outlander mercenaries now? Great.
Everyone inside is either dead or dying. It's for your own safety.
Hey, where do you think you're going? The Western Catacombs are off limits.

... not an illusion. Or rather, it is a necessary illusion.' The ending of the words is ALMSIVI. Yes, child, any question about anything I preached? Or is there anything else you need? Oh, you're a freelance adventurer, yes? The ossuary is in desperate need of someone like you.
... not an illusion. Or rather, it is a necessary illusion.' The ending of the words is ALMSIVI. Yes, child, any question about anything I preached? Or is there anything else you need?
It seems we have mutual friends, %PCRace. Come, show me what glitters in the dark.

Yes, what is it? Make it quick. I have to finish this report before tomorrow or Indrasa will have my head. You know, she'd probably keep it on her desk as a warning to her next apprentice. At least there'd be no shortage of other skulls for company. My mother used to tell me that our ancestors are always watching, but I never truly believed her until I was posted here.
I have nothing more to say to you, outlander.
Please, leave me...
Yes, what is it? Are you a pilgrim to these halls?
How fares your investigation, outlander?

What is it, %PCRace? This better be important. I can't be bothered with trifles while the Devil of Red Mountain is breathing down my soldiers' necks. It's been a long night. Several lives were lost... protecting the dead, to protect the living. We live in strange times, outlander. Strange times... But enough of my rambling. What's your business at the Ossuary of Ayem?
I truly do not. Now, good day serjo.
Fine. If it will get you out of my hair, and out of my workshop. Take these few Dwarven coins for services rendered. That should be suitable, yes? Good... Now, begone.

I would hardly call you a champion. You hunted down a single spider centurion in the catacombs. We would have managed to do it ourselves eventually. You've also surely damaged the device beyond repair in the process of retrieving the tube, so the best we can hope for is to salvage the spider for scrap.
Oh, you're still here? Is the gratitude of the Clockwork God not reward enough for you?!
Then begone with you!

Truly? The gears have aligned in my favor! One of our members witnessed the runaway automaton scuttle off into the Eastern Catacombs, but I dare not ask the Order of Ghosts for any further help. The Prefect spurns our creations as necromantic abominations. Does she forget that we have the blessing of Lord Vehk themself?

Do you mock a disciple of the Clockwork God? The world is naught but gears and cogs to my eyes! It should have been a simple repair. But I have been vexed by the ancestors! One of the automatons ran away with our only remaining fuse. The part is of Acolyte make and not easily replaceable, unfortunately. I cannot restore power to the shrine without it.
If you're a pilgrim, then you've arrived at a most inopportune time, %PCRace. Our Lord's shrine has been darkened and ceased its divine rotations!

You've found it! I do believe you've earned yourself the honor of illuminating our Lord's shrine, %PCRace. Quickly now, place the Acolyte Tube in the fuse box beneath the central console and witness the pure glory and truth that is Clockwork!
Yes? Do you bring any news of the runaway automaton?
[The old lady gives me a curious and concerned look.] If you don't mind me asking, what brings you here today?
[You can hear Garry repeating sentences to himself.] Why now?
[You can hear Garry repeating sentences to himself.] Why this way?
[You can hear Garry repeating sentences to himself.] Why did she have to die?
[Airen Dara doesn't look *that* busy.]
Thanks. Ummm? Why are there three urns? This one has the remains of a guar? Oh... Sometimes I forget, what death means to the people outside the Ossuaries. I wish they know that death is not the end.
Thanks.
Just put them down. I am quite busy at the moment.
Have you asked the lady to sign the form yet?
Good, here is the... Wait, did you just say no? You need to understand that this is a pressing matter. Talk to me as soon as whatever task at hand is completed.
Nice to meet you, %PCRank %PCName. I am Adansa's assistant Airen Dara. I handle most of the documents, reports, logs, and reminders here. Are you here for the new duty assignment?
What brings you to the Hall of Ghosts, %PCRank? Have you been lax in your duties?

Greetings outlander. I am Adansa Kren, Commander of the Order of Ghosts. We don't often get visitors down here, so I wonder... What is it that has brought you here, outlander? Do you mean to embark upon the Pilgrimage of the Dead?
This is the Great Hall of the Ossuary of Ayem, pilgrim. The Services tower is in the north wing and the shrine is in the Temple to the south.
This is the Ossuary of Ayem, pilgrim. What can I do for you?
Are you on pilgrimage here? What do you think of the Dwemer workshop?
If you're going into the Eastern Catacombs, stay away from the Dwemer ruins. Our scout said they're not safe anymore.
Are you on a pilgrimage here? Have you seen the statue outside? It is magnificent.
Are you on a pilgrimage here? Be sure to bring a torch or a lantern if you are going into the catacombs.
We have a small dining hall downstairs if you want a place to sit and eat.
The pomegranate trees outside the shrine grow from ashes. A rare sight of greenery in the dry ashlands.
Are you on a pilgrimage here?

These are the Southern Catacombs of the Ghostfence. I'll answer any questions, if I can. Perhaps you want directions to some specific place nearby? The Ossuary of Ayem is to the west and the Ossuary of Seht is to the east.

These are the Southern Catacombs, %PCName. Let me know if you need information. And if you have any news, or the latest rumors, please share them. We get few visitors here. While you're in the main hallway, please don't harm the cleaning centurions. They won't bother you.
You have come to the Southern Catacombs, pilgrim. There are no services down here. Head towards the west to the Ossuary of Ayem or east to the Ossuary of Seht if you want a place to rest.
I'll be happy to answer any questions, %PCName. Just tell me if you are looking for a specific place here.
Yes, %PCName. I can help you if you are on a pilgrimage here.
Necromancy is an abomination to our ancestors. All true Dunmer worship their ancestors, and honor their traditions. But the false gods won't let them rest in peace.
I am a scribe in the Order of Ghosts. My apprentice is Brelyna Hleran.
I am a scribe in the Order of Ghosts.
I am a Guardian of the Acolytes of Clockwork.

I am the head priest of the Ossuary of Ayem. My family hails from Mournhold, home to the Blessed Mother herself! We have served the Temple faithfully for generations, but I am the first of my name to be stationed on Vvardenfell. It is an... interesting place, don't you think?
I am the Commander of the Order of Ghosts.
I am the Prefect of the Ossuary of Seht.
I am the Prefect of the Ossuary of Vehk.
I am the Prefect of the Ossuary of Ayem.
We've already discussed my background in detail, and I would rather not get into it again.

Ah, yes... "What is an Altmer doing in a sacred Temple order?" you want to ask. You have the same perplexed look as all of the other pilgrims, though you are the first outlander pilgrim we've had in a long time. Well if you must hear my tale, go ahead and ask. But please do it quickly...
I am a %Rank in the Order of Ghosts.
To perform the Pilgrimage of the Dead, you must travel to the Great Ossuary of Ayem, the Great Ossuary of Seht, and the Great Ossuary of Vehk.
He should be working at the desk outside my office.
Airen Dara is the one working all day at his desk in the hall.
He is in the Hall of Ghosts, which can be accessed from Tower of Dawn.
Lonely lady lives in the Yahaz Hut. There.
The old lady lives in the hut right next to the silt strider port.
Ghostgate is garrisoned by the Ordinators and the Buoyant Armigers, House Redoran maintains a hostel for pilgrims, and the Order of Ghosts has its stronghold beneath the Tower of Dawn.

The Western Catacombs connect Ayem and Vehk. The Eastern Catacombs connect Vehk and Seht. The Southern Catacombs connect Ayem and Seht, and also have a connection here at Ghostgate. A few ancestral tombs both inside and outside the Ghostfence also have connections too.

The catacombs are dark - very dark - that’s the first thing you need to know about them. They also have their fair share of undead patrolling them as well. They go deep beneath Red Mountain to avoid its lava passages and are multi-purposed, but our order primarily uses them to travel between the Great Ossuaries and the Ghostgate.

You'd best be cautious if entering either of the catacombs here at Vehk. From the reports I've received, the Southern Catacombs still remain safe. However, it seems the Eastern and Western Catacombs are becoming more perilous by the day.
We sometimes do our training exercises down in the catacombs themselves, but there's honestly not much action there. The dead don't bother us, especially when we are in our full ceremonial kit.
I don't really mind the catacombs that much. The dead make sure you never feel lonely, but they also don't bother you with mindless chatter.

The Southern and Western Catacombs are mostly safe in the main halls. The ancestors prefer to remain undisturbed in the side crypts with the travelers coming and going. The Eastern Catacombs are a different story. Seht doesn't have the capacity to garrison a large force, and Vehk has been understaffed for years. As such, we've had to overly rely upon the ancestral centurions of the Acolytes to defend that portion of the catacombs. The centurions are far less... amicable... than other forms of undead.

I don't know why the Ghosts insist upon storing so many of the sacred ancestors' remains down there. I would much prefer we rebuild the old abbey in the wilted forest behind the ossuary. It could provide a great amount of storage for many more remains and offerings for the departed.
Oh, I don't know... perhaps the hordes of restless ancestors roaming the halls down there? The Ghosts keep the undead out of the main halls of the ossuary and that suits me just fine.
I wouldn't go down there if I were you. That place gives me the creeps.

If you're on a pilgrimage, it would be best to keep out of the Eastern Catacombs. Those foul Clockwork constructs gather there in much greater numbers than they do in the Southern Catacombs. It shames the Order of Ghosts that they need to rely upon these abominations so heavily.

I've tried to convey to the Ghosts the folly that they engage in by insisting on carrying simple torches and lanterns down there. True, our Dwemer-make ones are heavier, but they last longer and burn far brighter. And we've only ever had two explode on us. Perfectly safe by any reasonable standard.

The southern portion of the catacombs are much better patrolled and maintained by the Order than the eastern and western arms. The connection it provides between Ald'ruhn and the Ghostgate is invaluable.
Even with the defeat of Dagoth Ur, we will need to watch this section of the catacombs closely. There are still many blighted beasts that now have access to the catacombs through Kogoruhn.
The Ghosts must be more vigilant than ever, now that the enemy has broken through into the Western Catacombs. One mistake, and we could be overrun.

The Western Catacombs are built directly underneath Red Mountain, and they run its entire length from north to south. Fortunately, the only access points to the Western Catacombs are at the Ossuaries of Ayem and Vehk.

They are very convenient for travel between here and Ald'ruhn. Feel free to make use of the catacombs as a pilgrim or as a traveler as often as you wish. Just refrain from disturbing the offerings to the dead, or the Ghosts will have more than one bone to pick with you.
The catacombs can be accessed through the Hall of Ghosts, here at Ghostgate.
The catacombs are accessed deep below the ossuary in the bone pit. You can take the Western Catacombs to travel north to Vehk, or the Southern Catacombs to travel east to Ghostgate and Seht.
The Ossuary of Vehk is at the northern end of both the Western and Eastern Catacombs. You can access the catacombs from the large doors on either side of this hall.

To enter the catacombs, head outside using the door on the lower level of the Shrine. Head across the bridge, and into the Hall of the Order. You can use the large doors on either side of the hall to access the catacombs.
The Eastern Catacombs connect to a lower portion of the large Dwemer complex above. We often send scavenging parties down there, and the ruins provide ample basic materials for our research.
The doors to the catacombs are on either side of the Shrine of the Altar. Just head down the stairs in the main hall and you should find them.

House Redoran maintains a hostel with beds, food, and sundries in the Tower of Dusk. Redoran also offers services here for retainers and kin. The Temple and the Order of Ghosts have healers and other services in the Tower of Dawn.

Do not pity me for the life I have led, outlander. I have fought for my entire life to get to where I am today. I am a Commandant of the Order of Ghosts. I answer only to my Prefect, my Commander, and of course to Almsivi. My life may not look like much to you, but I am proud of who I am and who I have become, and I serve the Order, and my Gods, faithfully.

I was hidden away on his plantation until I reached the age of six. When I was old enough that the Order might accept me and train me, he had me shipped off to the Ghostgate. Commander Kren took one look at me and was ready to have me sent off to Ald'ruhn to fend for myself, but Prefect Ramoran was on official business at Ghostgate at the time and took pity on me. He took me in, and became the closest thing I have to a real father. I have lived here in the Ossuary of Vehk, and in the catacombs, ever since.

My father, a minor Hlaalu noble, needed to find a way to dispose of the bastard created from his 'union' with his High Elven concubine. He also needed to do this without killing said bastard, as his Imperial contacts might frown upon the killing of an innocent boy if it ever got out. He had the brilliant idea to gift me to a Temple order, and what better place to send me than to an order operating far away from Narsis, in the middle of Vvardenfell, where no one might ever find his illegitimate son.

First thing's first. Let me make one thing perfectly clear. I am not an outlander. At least, I don't consider myself one. Others within my nation may not be so generous. My mother is an Altmer, but I have lived my entire life in Morrowind, and my father is a Dunmer. A vile, wretch of a Dunmer, but a Dunmer nonetheless.
You're back. Good. Before you take on more duties, remember to check your advancement in our ranks.
You're back. Great. Give the urns to Airen. He will handle the rest. In the meantime, I have new duties for you, regarding the recent reports of small bones of irregular shape found in the remains.
We need someone to collect some of the remains of the recently deceased. Get the details from my assistant Airen Dara. When it's done, report back to me.
